thread:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary deploy stuck: rollout 'reframe-api-v2' at 12% in prod/us-west-2 failed healthchecks for new pods. Auto-rollback threshold not met. Paging on-call SRE.

oncall-devon: Acked. I'll take it — checking cluster now.

alex: saw a spike in 500s on /v1/generate at 10:12 UTC, traces point to transformer-worker pod oom/eviction. Link to dashboards: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/rollouts/reframe-api-v2?from=now-15m&to=now

maria: customers reporting errors in chat widgets, CS queue rising. @customer-success keeping an eye.

oncall-devon: grabbing logs. kubectl -n reframe get pods -l app=reframe-api, `kubectl logs -f reframe-api-v2-abcde -c reframe` shows repeated "kv cache miss" then OOMKilled.

ops-bot: Note: automatic canary rollback rule "healthcheck-failure-3m" was ON but mis-evaluated due to missing healthcheck tag on pods created by canary controller.

alex: so automated rollback didn't trigger. We need manual rollback / kill-switch. Recommend feature-flag kill first (fast) then rollback if needed.

oncall-devon: Agreed. What is the ff name?

maria: Feature flag is `reframe_v2_canary` in LaunchDarkly. I've got access. CS: which customers impacted? small subset on dedicated routing to us-west-2 only.

customer-success: ~7 orgs reporting increased errors, highest severity on one customer (acme-corp). They're experiencing request timeouts. Keeping them updated.

oncall-devon: I'm going to flip the kill switch now to stop routing traffic to the canary. Maria can you standby to confirm traffic drop?

maria: Standing by.

oncall-devon: @alex, @maria executing: (in LaunchDarkly) set reframe_v2_canary = false for prod/us-west-2 targeting rule.

maria: I see immediate decline in new canary pod creates. Traffic to canary pods drops from ~12% to 0.5% within 45s. Good.

alex: Nice. Also pinning route: set routing policy to prefer stable model variant. `routectl set-route reframe-api --version stable --region us-west-2` (telemetry shows routing shift).

oncall-devon: Starting manual rollback to previous replicaset to be safe. Command: `kubectl -n reframe rollout undo deployment/reframe-api --to-revision=42`

ops-bot: WARNING: rollback will restart 3 pods on each AZ. Expect short-lived increased latency ~30-60s.

oncall-devon: Proceeding.

alex: Watching pods come up. New pods (rs=42) become Ready at 10:20 UTC. Healthchecks passing for 3 successive probes.

maria: CS: noise dropping. acme-corp reporting partial recovery. Thank you.

oncall-devon: Running synthetic checks: `for z in {a,b,c}; do curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\\n" https://us-west-2.reframe/api/healthz; done` -> all 200s.

sre-lead: Quick note: we'll keep canary disabled until root cause triage. Ops, can we capture a full canary pod image and resource metrics?

alex: Already saved pod YAML and heap/profile artifacts: s3://ci-artifacts/reframe/canary/1770001111/ . I'll attach diff of container resources — looks like memory request was unchanged but RSS spiked due to kv cache growth.

maria: LaunchDarkly kill-switch is still off (false). Leaving it off. We should add a short-term guardrail to prevent re-enabling until RCA done.

oncall-handover: Handoff time — I'm getting pulled into another pager in 20m. @sre-lead, can you take next on-call? I'll write steps in the incident doc.

sre-lead: Taking it. Please paste the command sequence for rollback verification before you go.

oncall-devon: Paste:
```
# verify no canary traffic
kubectl -n reframe get svc reframe-api -o yaml | grep canary
# check pod statuses
kubectl -n reframe get pods -l app=reframe-api -o wide
# healthcheck
curl -I https://us-west-2.reframe/api/healthz
# tail logs
kubectl -n reframe logs -l app=reframe-api --since=10m | grep "OOMKilled\\|kv cache" -n
```

oncall-handover: Added that to the incident page: https://incidents.redwood/internal/1770001111. Leaving now, @sre-lead please ack.

sre-lead: Acked. I'll drive RCA and make a follow-up action list. Initial plan: a) patch canary controller to add healthcheck tag, b) add guardrail to LaunchDarkly targeting, c) add metric alarm for kv-cache growth.

customer-success: Looping in acme-corp with update: we rolled back suspected canary, traffic normalized. They'll verify on their side and escalate if needed.

alex: One more note — the canary image included a new kv-cache switch defaulting to enabled with no eviction policy preset. That's likely the memory growth trigger. We'll revert that flag in next build.

maria: Can we mark customer impact window? First error spike 10:12 UTC, resolved by routing/rollback by 10:21 UTC. Impact ~9 minutes, ~28 req/s errors peak, ~7 orgs affected.

sre-lead: Adding postmortem owner: @alex. Postmortem draft due EOD tomorrow. Action items assigned in the incident doc.

ops-bot: Incident severity set to Sev2. Incident state: Mitigated.

oncall-devon: Thanks team, handing off. If anyone re-enables canary, please ping this thread.

maria: Leaving note for Product: Please don't re-enable canary without explicit sign-off from SRE and product — adding to the PR checklist.

alex: I'll open the PR to revert kv-cache default and add eviction policy. Linking PR in incident doc.

customer-success: Great, will send a short customer-facing note summarizing timeline.

sre-lead: Closing loop: we'll run a canary replay in staging with cache settings and add an automated rollback test to prevent missing healthcheck tags.

oncall-handover: final: thanks everyone, handing over monitoring to @sre-lead.

deploy-bot: Deployment event closed: reframe-api-v2 manual rollback -> revision 42.

sre-lead: Incident thread closed but keeping doc open for RCA and action tracking.
